The restriction is mutual, lasts one year, covers only staff dealt with on the Purpose and excludes responses to public job postings, but the playbook has no exception for any of these. The rest of the NDA passes the playbook: it is mutual; the term is 2 years (within 3); confidentiality survives 3 years (within 5); all five exclusions are present (4.1–4.5); permitted disclosures are standard; Section 6 lets copies required by law and automatic back-ups be kept; remedies are limited to injunctive relief, with no liquidated damages; there is no non-compete or residuals clause; DIFC law and the DIFC Courts are acceptable; and the NDA is in English only, so the translation check does not apply. issues.quote: Each Party may freely use general skills, knowledge and experience, including information retained in the unassisted memory of its employees, for any purpose
issues.reason: Clause 9 is a residuals clause. It lets either Party use Confidential Information kept in its employees' unassisted memory 'for any purpose', so it is not limited to the Purpose. The playbook treats a residuals clause allowing use for any purpose as RESIDUALS_BROAD (YELLOW), so counsel needs to review it. The other checks pass: the NDA is mutual; the term is 2 years (limit 3); confidentiality survives 3 years (limit 5) and has no perpetual element; all five standard exclusions are in clauses 4.1–4.5; permitted disclosures are standard; return or destruction allows keeping copies required by law and back-up copies; the only remedy is injunctive relief, with no liquidated damages; there is no non-solicitation, non-compete or exclusivity; the governing law and forum are DIFC and the DIFC Courts, which are approved. The NDA is in English only, so the translation check does not apply.

issues.quote: The obligations of confidentiality survive indefinitely after the end of this Agreement.
issues.reason: Clause 7 keeps all confidentiality obligations in force with no end date. The playbook allows survival of up to 5 years after the end of the agreement, and protection without end is RED. Ruling R-2026-02 does not help: it only accepts open-ended protection for trade secrets, as long as they stay trade secrets. This clause covers all Confidential Information, not just trade secrets. Everything else meets the playbook: the agreement is mutual; the term is 2 years, under the 3-year limit; all five exclusions are there (clauses 4.1–4.5); permitted disclosures are standard; copies kept by law and in back-ups are allowed (clause 6); remedies are injunctive relief only; there is no non-solicit, non-compete or residuals clause; DIFC law and DIFC Courts are accepted; and the NDA is in English only, so the bilingual check does not apply. Routing: full legal review. Send this triage and the NDA to Legal for final confirmation before signing.

issues.quote: This Agreement has an initial term of five (5) years and renews automatically for successive periods of one (1) year unless either Party gives thirty (30) days' written notice of non-renewal.
issues.reason: Under ruling R-2026-01, the initial term is what counts against the three-year limit when either Party can stop renewal by notice. Here the initial term is five years, which is more than three. The one-year renewals can be stopped by notice, so they are not a separate problem. Counsel review is needed. A one-word fix would be to change 'five (5)' to 'three (3)'. Everything else passes: the agreement is mutual; confidentiality survives for 3 years, within the 5-year limit; all five standard exclusions are there (clauses 4.1 to 4.5); permitted disclosures are standard; the return-or-destruction clause lets each side keep copies required by law and back-up copies; remedies are limited to injunctive relief, with no liquidated damages; there is no non-solicit, non-compete, exclusivity or residuals clause; the governing law is DIFC with the DIFC Courts as forum, which is acceptable. The NDA is in English only, so it cannot have a translation mismatch. Next step: send this triage and the NDA to Legal for final confirmation before signing.

issues.reason: The initial term of three years is within the playbook limit. However, the Agreement renews automatically for further three-year periods, and neither Party can stop the renewal by notice. In practice the Agreement could run with no end date, so the three-year survival period after the end might never start. Suggested fix for counsel: add a right for either Party to stop renewal by written notice before the end of the current period.
